subject: Passing a Variance-Covariance Matrix for Random Effects in TMB

messages.author: 1240b60d4715a67c
messages.subject: Passing a Variance-Covariance Matrix for Random Effects in TMB
parts:
Hi all,

I’m new to TMB and was wondering if there is a proper way to pass a variance-covariance matrix for random effects in a linear mixed model (y=Xb + Zu + e), with :

  • u∼N(0,sigma2A)

  • e∼N(0,sigma2Id)

Where:

  • u is the vector of random effects.

  • e is the vector of residuals.

  • A is the genetic relationship matrix (variance-covariance matrix for u).

  • Id is the identity matrix for e.

I am working on a model where I want to include a variance-covariance matrix (A) for random effects, specifically the genetic relationship matrix A, which represents relationships between individuals.

I’ve been working with simulated data, and when A is an identity matrix, the code below works well. The correlation between the true and estimated u is consistently high (r≈0.91+).

However, when I use a structured A (which was also used to simulate the data), the correlation between the true and estimated u becomes poor.

Does anyone have insights into why this might be happening? I would appreciate any advice or suggestions for addressing this issue.


Below is the TMB model code:


Type objective_function<Type>::operator() (){

/*-------------------------------Data--------------------------------------*/

DATA_VECTOR(y); // vector of observations

DATA_MATRIX(X); // Design matrix for fixed effects

DATA_MATRIX(Z); // Design matrix for random effects

DATA_MATRIX(Id); // Identity matrix for errors

DATA_MATRIX(A); // Variance-covariance matrix (genetic relationship matrix)


/*-----------------------------------Parameters-----------------------------*/

PARAMETER_VECTOR(beta); // vector of fixed effects (b)

PARAMETER_VECTOR(u); //vector of randoms effects

PARAMETER(log_sd_u);

PARAMETER(log_sd_e);


/*----------------------------local variales -------------------*/

// size

int n = y.size(); //length of y

int q = A.cols(); // number of random effects


/*----------------------------nll-----------------------------*/

Type nll = Type(0.0);


/*----------------------------contribution to the nll-----------------------*/

// Contribution of the observations

vector<Type> m(n);

m = X * beta + Z*u;

MVNORM_t<Type> mvn_y_cor(Id);

vector<Type> vec_sd(n);

vec_sd.fill(exp(log_sd_e));

nll += VECSCALE(mvn_y_cor, vec_sd)(y - m);


// contribution of randoms effects

MVNORM_t<Type> mvn_u_cor(A);

vector<Type> sd_u(q);

sd_u.fill(exp(log_sd_u));

nll += VECSCALE(mvn_u_cor, sd_u)(u);


return nll;

}


Thank you in advance for your help!


--

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: Passing a Variance-Covariance Matrix for Random Effects in TMB
parts:
You are passing A as a general matrix, however there has to be a positive definite constraint.
It's probably easiest to use the UNSTRUCTURED_CORR class as described here:
https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/_book/Densities.html#multivariate-normal-distributions
